'''Molly S. Shoichet''' {{post-nominals|FRS}} is a Canadian science professor at the [[University of Toronto]] specializing in chemistry, biomaterials and biomedical engineering. She was Ontario's first Chief Scientist.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.utoronto.ca/news/molly-shoichet-named-ontario-s-first-chief-scientist|title=Molly Shoichet named Ontario's first Chief Scientist|website=University of Toronto News|access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-doug-ford-fires-ontarios-chief-scientist/|title=PCs dismiss Ontario's chief scientist amid broad effort to undo Liberals' legacy|date=4 July 2018|access-date=19 April 2019|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|last1=Giovannetti |first1=Justin }}</ref> Shoichet is a biomedical engineer known for her work in [[tissue engineering]], and is the only person to be a fellow of the three [[National Academies]] in Canada.

== Education ==
Shoichet studied at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and received her bachelor's degree in chemistry in 1987. She attended the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]] for her doctoral studies and earned her PhD in polymer science and engineering in 1992.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title = The Shoichet Lab {{!}} Molly's Bio|url = http://www.ecf.utoronto.ca/~molly/molly_bio.html|website = www.ecf.utoronto.ca|access-date = 4 August 2015}}</ref>

== Career ==
After receiving her doctorate, Shoichet joined the faculty of [[Brown University]] as an [[adjunct professor]], while simultaneously working in industry. Shoichet joined the [[University of Toronto Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering]] in 1995, where she remains as of 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Molly Shoichet |url=https://bme.utoronto.ca/faculty-research/core-faculty/molly-shoichet/ |website=University of Toronto |publisher=Institue of Biomedical Engineering {{!}} Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering |access-date=January 14, 2026}}</ref> Her work includes tissue and polymer engineering, focusing on drug delivery and tissue regeneration. Early in her career, she studied the [[blood–brain barrier]].<ref name=":0" /> Her lab's methods involve using a [[gel]] to deliver drugs to a specific location in the central nervous system and to bypass the blood-brain barrier. The drugs delivered in this way include [[chemotherapy]] drugs and agents to slow or reverse damage from a stroke. This delivery method is also being tested with stem cells,<ref>{{cite web|title = Canadian researcher Molly Shoichet wins L'Oreal/UNESCO For Women in Science Award|url = http://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/canadian-researcher-molly-shoichet-wins-l-oreal-unesco-for-women-in-science-award-1.2979938|access-date = 4 August 2015|publisher=CBC}}</ref> and include studies on the use of [[hydrogels]] that deliver stem cells to nonfunctioning [[retina]]s.<ref>{{cite news|title = Injectable gel makes inroads against blindness and stroke|url = https://www.theglobeandmail.com/technology/science/injectable-gel-makes-inroads-against-blindness-and-stroke/article24442521/|work=Globe & Mail| date=14 May 2015 |access-date = 4 August 2015| last1=Semeniuk | first1=Ivan }}</ref> These hydrogels are designed to be easily injectable into the tissue and they then form a scaffold for cells to grow in the appropriate three-dimensional shape.<ref>{{cite web|title = Molly Shoichet Receives TERMIS Senior Scientist Award|url = http://www.chem-eng.utoronto.ca/news/feature/Molly_Shoichet_Receives_TERMIS_Senior_Scientist_Award.htm|website = chem-eng.utoronto.ca|access-date = 4 August 2015}}</ref>

In 2015, Shoichet co-founded [[Research2Reality]] to showcase scientific research in Canada through a combination of accessible blog posts and short videos.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.universityaffairs.ca/features/feature-article/molly-shoichet-sciences-symphony-conductor/|title=Molly Shoichet, science's symphony conductor|website=University Affairs|date=February 2019 |language=en-US|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref> She has also curated the "Artful Science" exhibit at the [[Toronto Pearson International Airport]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/listen/shows/metro-morning/segment/15612504|title=Metro Morning {{!}} New art and science exhibit at Pearson Airport|website=CBC Listen|language=en|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thevarsity.ca/2018/09/30/artful-science-exhibit-takes-off-at-toronto-pearson-airport/|title=Artful Science exhibit takes off at Toronto Pearson Airport|date=30 September 2018|website=The Varsity|access-date=5 February 2019}}</ref>

In November 2017, Shoichet was named as Ontario's first Chief Scientist by then Premier [[Kathleen Wynne]].<ref name=":1" /> She was leading a team of six to build connections between the federal government, science and business sectors, and promote the use of evidence in policy development.<ref name=":3" />

On 3 July 2018, Shoichet was dismissed from her position by the newly elected Conservative government of Ontario<ref name=":2" /> when the office of chief scientist was eliminated.<ref name=Semeniuk/>

== Honours and awards ==
In 2010, Shoichet was one of 30 people to be awarded the [[Order of Ontario]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news.ontario.ca/mci/en/2011/01/29-appointees-named-to-ontarios-highest-honour-1.html|title=30 Appointees Named To Ontario's Highest Honour|access-date=10 February 2010|date=21 January 2011}}</ref>

Shoichet was the North American recipient of the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science]] in 2015 for her work on regeneration of nerve tissue, and in developing direct drug delivery methods for the [[spinal cord]] and brain using novel materials. She has advocated for women in science and women professors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unesco.org/new/en/natural-sciences/priority-areas/gender-and-science/for-women-in-science-programme/2015-awards/|title=2015 L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|access-date=20 March 2015|publisher=UNESCO|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320212520/http://www.unesco.org/new/en/natural-sciences/priority-areas/gender-and-science/for-women-in-science-programme/2015-awards/|archive-date=20 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title = U of T biomedical engineer wins women in science prize|url = https://www.theglobeandmail.com/technology/science/uoft-biomedical-engineer-wins-women-in-science-prize/article23257964/|access-date = 4 August 2015|work=Globe & Mail| date=3 March 2015 }}</ref>

The University of Toronto designated her a "University Professor" in 2014. She is the only person to be a fellow of the three National Academies in Canada.<ref name=":0" /> The University of Toronto also honored her in 2013 as an "Inventor of the Year".<ref>{{cite web|title = Meet U of T's Inventors of the Year {{!}} U of T News|url = http://www.news.utoronto.ca/meet-u-ts-inventors-year|website = www.news.utoronto.ca|access-date = 4 August 2015}}</ref> She is the 2017 winner of the Kalev Pugi Award of the Chemical Institute of Canada.<ref>[http://www.cheminst.ca/awards/sci-canada-awards/kalev-pugi-award Kalev Pugi Award] Chemical Institute of Canada. Retrieved 18 December 2016.</ref> She holds the Canada Research Chair in Tissue Engineering.<ref name=":3" />

In 2017, she was also awarded the [[Izaak-Walton-Killam Award|Killam Prize]] for engineering.<ref>[http://www.cbc.ca/news/technology/killam-prize-winner-female-scientist-shoichet-1.4095439 Prestigious Killam Prize for engineering awarded to female scientist second year in a row] By Nicole Mortillaro, CBC News, 2 May 2017</ref> She was awarded Officer of the Order of Canada (OC) as per Government House of 29 December 2017.

In 2020, she was the winner of the [[Gerhard Herzberg Canada Gold Medal for Science and Engineering]], awarded by the [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council]] of Canada (NSERC).<ref>{{cite web |title=Molly Shoichet |url=https://www.nserc-crsng.gc.ca/Prizes-Prix/Herzberg-Herzberg/Profiles-Profils/Shoichet-Shoichet_eng.asp |website=NSERC Prizes. Gerhard Herzberg. Winners. |date=10 November 2020 |publisher=Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada |access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref><ref name=Semeniuk>{{cite web |last1=Semeniuk |first1=Ivan |title=University of Toronto researcher awarded Canada's top science prize |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-university-of-toronto-researcher-awarded-canadas-top-science-prize/ |publisher=The Globe and Mail (Canada) |date=11 November 2020 |access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref>

=== Other honours ===
* Fellow, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2013)
* [[Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal]] (2013)
* Fellow, [[Royal Society of Canada|Canadian Academy of Sciences of the Royal Society of Canada]]
* Fellow, [[Canadian Academy of Engineering]]
* Fellow, [[Canadian Academy of Health Sciences]]
* [[Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine International Society]] (TERMIS) Senior Scientist Award (2014)
* Fellow, [[Royal Society]] UK
* Fellow, [[National Academy of Inventors]]

== Personal life ==
Her brother, Brian Shoichet, is a professor at the University of California, San Francisco, where he serves as Co-Vice Dean of Graduate Pharmacy Education Programs and faculty in the Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry.
